summary: Defines several subcodes for the BGP Cease NOTIFICATION message. They give more detail about why a session was closed, helping operators match events and diagnose peering problems. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: When a friend hangs up, they say why: I have to go eat, or my phone is dying. It helps you know what happened.

subtitle: Eight reason codes that let a BGP router say why it is closing a session, plus advice on how to retry.

tldr.problem: A BGP Cease NOTIFICATION message told the neighbor that a session was being closed but not why, which made it hard for operators to correlate network events and diagnose peering problems.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4486 defines eight subcodes for the Cease error code, such as Administrative Shutdown and Out of Resources, says when a speaker should send each one, and recommends a retry backoff after some of them.
tldr.outcome: Operators get a reason with every Cease. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has since been updated by RFC 8203 and RFC 9003.

facts.label: Future assignments
facts.value: Standards Action or Early IANA Allocation

today: RFC 4486 is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 8203 and RFC 9003; it has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why Cease Needs Reasons
sections.content:
A BGP speaker that wants to end a session with a neighbor sends a NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Cease. On its own, that code does not say what led to the shutdown. RFC 4486 adds more detail so that network operators can correlate network events and diagnose BGP peering issues.

The document does two things. It defines several subcodes for the Cease NOTIFICATION message, and it recommends that a speaker use a backoff mechanism when it retries a BGP connection after receiving a Cease with certain subcodes.
sections.eli5: Hanging up without a word leaves the other side guessing. This document gives routers a short list of reasons to say out loud before they hang up.

sections.title: The Eight Subcodes
sections.content:
Section 3 defines eight subcodes for the Cease NOTIFICATION message, numbered 1 to 8. Each one has a symbolic name that describes the cause of the shutdown: Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached, Administrative Shutdown, Peer De-configured, Administrative Reset, Connection Rejected, Other Configuration Change, Connection Collision Resolution and Out of Resources.

The names split into a few families. Some are operator choices (shutdown, de-configuration, reset, other configuration change), some are protocol events (a prefix limit hit, a connection collision) and some are refusals or resource problems (connection rejected, out of resources).
sections.eli5: It is a menu of eight reasons for hanging up, each with a number, like a list of excuses on a card that both sides have a copy of.

sections.title: When Each Subcode Is Sent
sections.content:
Section 4 says when a speaker sends each subcode, and how strongly. Only the first is a MUST.

  • Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached: if the speaker ends the peering because the number of address prefixes received from the neighbor exceeds a locally configured upper bound, it MUST send this subcode.
  • Administrative Shutdown, Peer De-configured, Administrative Reset, Connection Rejected and Other Configuration Change: the speaker SHOULD send the matching subcode when it shuts down, de-configures or resets the peering, or disallows a connection after accepting the transport connection (for example, because the peer is not configured locally).
  • Connection Collision Resolution: SHOULD be used when the Cease results from the collision resolution procedure in RFC 4271.
  • Out of Resources: the speaker MAY send it when it runs out of resources such as memory and decides to reset a session.
sections.eli5: Some reasons the router must always give, some it should give, and one it may give if it is too overwhelmed to explain much.

sections.title: The Optional Prefix-Limit Data
sections.content:
For the Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached subcode, the message MAY carry extra detail in its Data field. The data consists of the Address Family Information, defined in the multiprotocol extensions for BGP-4, and the upper bound that was exceeded.

The layout, shown in Figure 1 of the RFC, is an AFI of 2 octets, a SAFI of 1 octet and a prefix upper bound of 4 octets. The meaning and use of the AFI and SAFI pair is the same as in Section 7 of RFC 2858.
sections.eli5: When the reason is too many routes, the router can add a note saying which kind of routes and what the limit was.

sections.title: Retrying After a Cease
sections.content:
The RFC also gives advice on what to do on the receiving side. It is RECOMMENDED that a speaker behave as though the DampPeerOscillations attribute from RFC 4271 were true for the peer when it retries a BGP connection after receiving a Cease with the subcode Administrative Shutdown, Peer De-configured, Connection Rejected or Out of Resources.

An implementation SHOULD also impose an upper bound on the number of consecutive automatic retries. Once the bound is reached, it would stop retrying until some administrative intervention, that is, setting the AllowAutomaticStart attribute to FALSE.

The point of the backoff is to stop two routers from hammering each other with reconnection attempts when one side has said it is gone, rejecting the connection or out of resources.
sections.eli5: If someone tells you they are not coming to the phone, you should wait longer between calls and eventually stop calling until a grown-up says it is fine.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: The document defines subcodes 1 to 8 for the BGP Cease NOTIFICATION message. Future assignments are to be made using either the Standards Action process defined in RFC 2434 or the Early IANA Allocation process defined in RFC 4020. An assignment consists of a name and a value.
sections.eli5: A keeper of the list hands out new numbers only after careful approval, so no two reasons share a number.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security section is a single sentence: this extension to BGP does not change the underlying security issues inherent in the existing BGP. The RFC adds no new protection and describes no new attack.
sections.eli5: Giving a reason for hanging up does not make the phone line any safer or any less safe than it already was.

items.label: Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached
items.desc: Received prefixes exceeded a locally configured upper bound; sending is a MUST.

items.label: Administrative Shutdown
items.desc: The speaker administratively shuts down the peering.

items.label: Administrative Reset
items.desc: The speaker administratively resets the peering.

items.label: Connection Rejected
items.desc: A connection is disallowed after the transport connection was accepted.

items.label: Other Configuration Change
items.desc: A reset caused by a configuration change not covered above.

items.label: Connection Collision Resolution
items.desc: The Cease results from collision resolution.

items.label: Out of Resources
items.desc: The speaker runs out of resources such as memory and resets a session.
